New York · Wed Nov 18 – Sun Nov 22, 2026

Four nights of Manhattan after dark

Slow mornings, two daytime outings (the Intrepid on Thursday and the Brooklyn Bridge on Friday), your three fixed evenings, and a hidden bar after the show and after the steak dinner. Everything starts and ends at Deb's place on 9th Avenue, so most of it is a short walk or a ten-minute cab. Every stop has a Plan B underneath it, something close by to swap in if it's booked or you change your mind. Everything is booked ahead where it can be; the few walk-in bars are marked, so you know where a wait is possible.

Wednesday, Nov 18

Arrival night
10:29p

Land at JFK, cab straight to Deb's

Take the yellow-cab line, not a hailing driver inside the terminal. JFK to Manhattan is a flat fare plus tolls and surcharges, so expect roughly $90–110 with tip. At that hour it's 40–50 minutes to 9th Ave & 38th.

Thursday, Nov 19

Your own day · Tavola at 5 · the show at 7
9:30a

Sleep in, then breakfast to go at Fresh From Hell

No alarm needed. Leave Deb's around 9:30 and walk 8 blocks up 9th Avenue to Fresh From Hell, a juice-and-smoothie counter that is right on your way to the Intrepid. Everything is made in front of you: açai bowls with house granola, creamy coconut oatmeal, Greek yogurt with fruit, toasted sprouted bagels with a cashew cream cheese they make themselves, cold-pressed juices and smoothies. Order at the counter, take it with you and eat on the walk west.

9th Ave between 46th & 47thCounter service · order ahead online

Delivery runs from 7am; I couldn't confirm the counter's opening time, so check Google Maps the night before.

Menu and order ahead
Plan B if it's closed or you want a different grab-and-go
  • Pure Ktchn, 352 W 46th (8th–9th Aves). A vegan counter with açai bowls with granola and green smoothies, open 9am to 9pm Monday to Saturday per its listing. 2 minutes off your route.
  • Gotham West Market, 600 11th Ave. A food hall a few blocks from the pier with coffee and breakfast counters; it opens early (listings say 7:30am).
10:30a

Intrepid Museum and the Space Shuttle Enterprise

The ship you were thinking of is the Intrepid, an aircraft carrier turned museum at Pier 86; the shuttle on board is the Enterprise, NASA's first orbiter, in its own pavilion on the flight deck. Book a 10:30 entry and give it about two and a half hours: the shuttle pavilion, the jets on deck, the hangar deck exhibits.

Pier 86, W 46th St & 12th Ave · 15-min walk from Fresh From Hell10am–5pm · adults about $32 online

The museum's own site says the Exploreum (the flight simulators and 4D experience) closes at 3pm on Thursday, Nov 19, so a morning entry is the right call. Last entry is 4pm. The shuttle is not affected.

Buy timed tickets
Plan B / swap nearby
  • MoMA: Brancusi, The Artist and His Studio. The first big Brancusi retrospective in 30 years, about 210 sculptures, tools and photos from his Paris studio (through Feb 27). Book a timed ticket; the galleries get crowded. 11 W 53rd, 10-min cab. MoMA
  • Circle Line from Pier 83, next door to the Intrepid. The Landmarks cruise runs down the Hudson to the Statue of Liberty and back in about 90 minutes. Check sailing times for the day. Circle Line
1:15p

Lunch and the rest of the afternoon are yours

You'll be at the pier, so eat close and light. None of these need a booking. Then wander back at your own pace. Be at Deb's door by 4:45: Tavola is one block away, and your table is at 5:00, and it's a pasta-and-pizza dinner, so keep lunch healthy.

Healthy lunch, nearest the Intrepid first
  • Gotham West Market, 600 11th Ave (W 44th). A food hall about a 5-minute walk from the pier. Older write-ups list Indie Fresh (the healthy option), Choza Taqueria (salads and bowls) and Uma Temakeria (made-to-order sushi hand rolls), but the vendor list may have changed, so check when you walk in.
  • Pure Ktchn, 352 W 46th (8th–9th Aves). A vegan counter with açai bowls and green smoothies. Listed 9am to 9pm Monday to Saturday, and it's on the way back east.
  • Fresh From Hell, 9th Ave between 46th and 47th. If you didn't eat there this morning: sandwiches on good bread with vegetarian options, a build-your-own salad bar, warm and cold soups, fresh juices and smoothies, all made in front of you. Menu
If you want something to do (nothing here needs booking)
  • Circle Line from Pier 83, next to the Intrepid. The Landmarks cruise to the Statue of Liberty and back is about 90 minutes. Check sailing times for the day. Circle Line
  • Bryant Park Winter Village, as the lights come on around 4:15. About 180 kiosks around a rink, free to walk. A 15-minute cab from the pier, and 15 minutes back to Deb's. Winter Village
  • Hudson River Greenway. A flat walk south along the water from the pier to Hudson Yards, then 10 minutes east to Deb's.
5:00p

Dinner at Tavola, one block from Deb's

A Hell's Kitchen Italian place with a wood-burning oven: Sicilian, Apulian and Tuscan food, with wood-fired pizza and pasta, 4.2 stars on Yelp from about 1,680 reviews. It's dressed down, so nice but not fancy, and the tables are close together. Yelp tables run a 90-minute maximum, so a 5:00 seat has you finished by 6:30. Then it's a 20-minute walk or an 8-minute cab to The Town Hall; leave by 6:30.

BookedThu 5:00pm · 2 people488 9th Ave (37th–38th)(212) 273-1181
Backups, only if plans change
  • Joe Allen, 326 W 46th. Open since 1965 on Restaurant Row, brick walls covered in posters from Broadway flops, and used to getting people out before curtain. Book 5:30 on OpenTable, and leave by 6:35. Book
  • Becco, 355 W 46th. Lidia Bastianich's pre-theater place: a salad, then unlimited servings of the three pastas of the day. Fast and generous. Book on OpenTable
7:00p

Michelle Wolf: Best Job in the World

The Town Hall is a 1921 hall with famously good acoustics, which helps stand-up more than you'd think. Doors usually open 30 minutes before; arrive by 6:40 to get settled, which fits a 6:30 walk or cab from Tavola.

Bar Centrale, up the unmarked stairs

A 12-minute walk west along 46th Street. There's no sign: an unmarked door beside Joe Allen, then a flight of stairs to a small, dim room where Broadway actors drink after their shows. Book by phone; the bar closes at 11:30pm.

Friday, Nov 20

The bridge by day · at Deb's by 5 to help set up · Friendsgiving at 6
11:00a

Walk the Brooklyn Bridge, Brooklyn back to Manhattan

Walk it toward Manhattan, so the skyline is in front of you the whole way instead of behind you. Take the A or C from 34th St–Penn Station to High St in Brooklyn (about 20 minutes; leave Deb's at 10:30). Start with ten minutes in DUMBO: Washington St at Water St is the famous shot of the Manhattan Bridge framed between old warehouses. At 11, walk the 1.1 miles across on the raised wooden walkway, about 40 minutes with photo stops, and come off at City Hall.

Start: High St station (A/C) · End: Brooklyn Bridge–City HallFree · no booking

Weekday mornings are quieter on the bridge, and there's no line or ticket. You come off at City Hall around 11:50 with lunch below, and you must be back at Deb's by 5:00, so there is plenty of room. Sleep in: nothing happens before 10:30.

Plan B if it's raining
  • MoMA for the Brancusi show (timed tickets, book that morning). Cab from Deb's at 10:45, an hour and a quarter inside, then a 10-minute cab to Grand Central for lunch. MoMA
  • Or move the bridge to Sunday morning. Leave Deb's at 9, walk it, and you're back by noon for the 12:45 airport cab. Brunch becomes a coffee and something to go in DUMBO.
12:00p

Healthy lunch near the bridge

You come off the bridge at City Hall around 11:50 and the back-by-5 clock is easy. None of these need a booking. Listings and ratings come from aggregator pages, so check the address on Google Maps before you walk over.

Bowls and salads, by where you are
  • After the walk, near City Hall: Sweetgreen or Chopt on Chambers St (about 125 Chambers). Salads and warm grain bowls, a 5 to 8 minute walk from the City Hall end of the bridge. Listings disagree on which of the two is at that address; either works.
  • Before the walk, in DUMBO: Sweetgreen, 50 Washington St. Its Harvest Bowl and salmon bowl are the most-mentioned items. It's the same street as the Manhattan Bridge photo spot, so it fits if you'd rather eat before crossing.
  • In DUMBO Heights: Mulberry & Vine. A health-focused prepared-foods counter with a rotating set of bowls, about $12. Its listing is undated, so confirm it's open.
12:30p

Or a sit-down lunch at the Grand Central Oyster Bar (optional)

Lunch under the tiled vaults of the Oyster Bar, open since 1913; the pan roast is the classic order. On the way out, stand in opposite corners of the tiled arch outside its entrance and whisper into the wall. The other person hears you clearly 30 feet away.

Optional. Take this instead of a bowl if you want to sit down, an old-school bookable lunch. Skip it if you eat near the bridge.

Lower level, Grand Central · 10 min from City Hall on the 4/5Weekdays from 11:30am · closed weekends
Book on OpenTable212-490-6650
Plan B / swap nearby
  • No table: Cipriani Dolci, on the balcony above Grand Central's main concourse. Venetian food, a Bellini, and a view down onto the whole hall. Call (212) 973-0999 to book. You keep the Whispering Gallery either way: it's free and there's never a line.
  • Something else to see: the Chrysler Building lobby, a 3-minute walk east at Lexington & 42nd. The Art Deco lobby is all red marble, chrome and a painted ceiling, free on weekdays. The building recently changed hands and is up for renovation, so check the door is open.
1:45p

Free until 5:00

Nothing is booked here. If you want one more thing, the library tours below fit best, then the others. Whatever you pick, be on your way to Deb's by 4:30.

Only if you want more
  • The New York Public Library (Schwarzman Building), 5th Ave at 42nd. Every tour is free, and these are Friday's times:
    • 2:00pm, the full building tour. One hour with a docent, ending in the Rose Main Reading Room. It's the one that needs a ticket: limited to 20 people, booked online, with the week's tickets released on Sunday (Nov 15), so check for a seat today. Meet at the Visitor Center. The other full tour is 11:00am, which clashes with the bridge. Book the tour
    • 1:30pm and 3:00pm, the 15-minute Rose Main Reading Room tour. No ticket: sign up in the McGraw Rotunda (3rd floor) 30 minutes before, first 25 people. If the 2:00 tour is full, this is your way into the room.
    • 12:30pm and 3:30pm, the Treasures exhibition tour. 45 minutes through the Polonsky Exhibition of some of the rarest items in the library's collections. Sign up at the exhibition entrance 15 minutes before, first 15 people.
    • Best fit with your day: the 2:00 tour if you get a ticket. If not, the 3:00 Reading Room tour (sign up at 2:30), then the 3:30 Treasures tour, then leave at 4:15. The Reading Room is also open to walk in from 10 to 11am, with the last entry at 10:50. Times are from NYPL's own page, read Nov 18.
  • SUMMIT One Vanderbilt, the mirrored observation deck beside Grand Central. Timed tickets only, so book a 2:00 or 2:30 slot online (about $45 plus extras); sunset slots sell out, but you won't be there at sunset. Allow 90 minutes. Book tickets
  • The Morgan Library, J.P. Morgan's 1906 private library, 10 minutes from Grand Central: three tiers of walnut bookcases and a painted ceiling. About $25, book a timed ticket. An hour is plenty. Tickets
  • The Chrysler Building lobby, 3 minutes from Grand Central. Free on weekdays, ten minutes is enough. Check that the door is open, since the building recently changed hands.
5:00p

At Deb's to help set up Friendsgiving

Be at the apartment by 5:00 so you can help. It's about 15 minutes by cab or a 25-minute walk from Grand Central, so leave by 4:30 if you're coming from there.

FixedDeb's place

Saturday, Nov 21

You + Deb's friend + Deb, all day
10:15a

Walk the High Line south

The north end starts at Hudson Yards, about ten minutes from Deb's. Walk the elevated park south for about 40 minutes, past the Chelsea galleries and between the buildings, all the way to the end at Gansevoort Street. Free, no line.

Enter at W 34th St & 12th Ave or Hudson YardsFree · opens 7am
High Line map
Plan B / swap nearby
  • Little Island, if you're ahead of schedule: a park on 132 concrete tulips over the Hudson, 5 minutes from the High Line's end. Free, no line in November. Little Island
  • The Whitney: artport, A History of Internet Art. Opens to the public this very day, Sat Nov 21, right at the High Line's south end. Book a timed ticket if you'd rather do art than the walk. Whitney
  • If it's cold or wet: The Met's Krasner and Pollock show. Buy timed tickets online, cab up at 10, then cab down to brunch. The Met
11:00a

Brunch at Pastis

Right where the High Line ends. A big, buzzy Paris-style brasserie with a zinc bar, white subway tiles and steak frites, croque monsieurs and good eggs. Sit-down and booked, so no food-hall lines. Ask for the check at 12:05 to make the show.

52 Gansevoort St, Meatpacking DistrictBook 11:00 for 3 · (212) 929-4844
Book Pastis
Plan B if Pastis is booked
  • The Standard Grill, 2 minutes away under the High Line at 848 Washington St. Weekend brunch from 11 in a wood-paneled room. Reservations through the hotel's site. Book
1:00p

The Christmas Spectacular with the Rockettes

The 1:00 matinee at Radio City Music Hall: the kick line, the wooden soldiers, a new number this year, and the 1932 Art Deco hall itself, which is worth the ticket alone. 90 minutes, no intermission. Cab from Pastis at 12:10 (about 20 minutes), and get there by 12:35, since there's a bag check at the door.

Radio City Music Hall, 1260 6th Ave at 50thBook 3 tickets · Sat shows: 10am, 1pm, 4pm, 7pm
Buy tickets
Plan B if 1:00 is sold out, or you'd rather skip the show
  • Take the 10:00am show and flip the day: Rockettes first, then cab down to a 12:00 brunch and walk the High Line after. Skating moves to a 3:30 slot.
  • Same building, no show: the Radio City Stage Door Tour. About an hour backstage at the hall. On Saturdays in the holiday season tours leave every 30 minutes between 10:30am and 4:00pm. It sells out in this season, so reserve a time ahead. Take the 1:00 or 1:30 and you still make the 2:45 skate. Enter through the Executive Entrance on 50th St. Book the tour
  • Top of the Rock, the observation deck on the same plaza as the rink. Timed tickets online: book a 1:00 or 1:30 entry, about an hour up top, and you are next to the rink for 2:45. Tickets
  • Free, no booking: walk Rockefeller Center's holiday decorations and 5th Avenue's store windows, and have a late lunch near the plaza. Don't count on the Saks Fifth Avenue windows and light show: they unveil Monday Nov 23, two days after you leave.
2:45p

Skate at The Rink at Rockefeller Center

Your one skate of the trip, right across the street from Radio City. No standing in line: book a timed General Skate slot (from about $22) or the new VIP Skate, which opened Nov 14 with the new Skate House. The tree usually arrives mid-November and stays dark until the lighting in early December, so expect scaffolding around it.

Rockefeller Plaza, 49th–50th StBook for 3 · 2:45pm slot
Reserve skate time
Plan B if it's sold out
  • Wollman Rink, Central Park, instead. Not a second skate, a swap. It's a bigger rink with the skyline over the trees, timed tickets online, and it's a few minutes' walk from the carriage line. Walk up 6th Ave after the show and book a 3:15 slot. Wollman tickets
4:15p

Horse-carriage ride through Central Park at sunset

Good news: the carriages are still running. Mayor Mamdani and the City Council did agree to end them, which is probably what you heard: the Council passed "Romanch's Law" 40–7 on Oct 22 and the mayor has said he'll sign it. But it phases the carriages out by June 1, 2028; nothing in it stops rides now. Walk up Fifth Avenue past St. Patrick's (about 15 minutes) to the carriage line on Central Park South. No booking: pick a driver, agree the route and the posted city fare before you get in, and ride into the 4:35 sunset.

Central Park South, 5th–6th AvesAbout 20–45 min · bring a scarf

This part of Central Park South is a block from Bourbon Steak, so you'll know the walk for tonight.

Plan B if the carriages aren't running, or you'd rather skip them
  • The Palm Court at The Plaza, at 5th & 59th, the same corner where the carriages line up. Holiday afternoon tea or a drink under the stained-glass skylight, with the park outside. Book a 4:15 table for 3 on OpenTable; holiday dates fill up, so reserve it now and cancel if you ride. Book · (212) 546-5300
  • The Grand Salon at the Baccarat Hotel, 28 W 53rd, if the Palm Court is full. A cream-and-crystal room lit by Baccarat chandeliers, cocktails and bites by the fire. Book on OpenTable; non-hotel guests have about a $75 per person minimum. 8 minutes from the rink. Book
  • A pedicab tour of Central Park, with blankets. A private ride in an open bike-taxi: the park without the horses. Operators sell private tours online, from about an hour; prices run from about $28 to $180 depending on the operator and length, so compare. Most want at least two riders, so check that it seats three, and service can pause in heavy rain. See a pedicab tour
  • Free, no booking: walk the park at sunset. Enter at 5th Ave and 59th, walk the Mall to Bethesda Terrace (about 20 minutes) and watch the 4:35 sunset from the arcade, then cab to Deb's to change.
5:15p

Back to Deb's to change

A 15-minute cab. Nearly two hours to rest and dress for dinner: jacket, no sneakers.

7:30p

Bourbon Steak New York

Michael Mina's steakhouse inside the 1931 Essex House, facing the park, so the carriage ride and dinner sit on the same block. Leave Deb's at 7:10. The bar and lounge stay open until 1am if dinner runs long.

Raines Law Room at The William, a table for four

About 15 minutes by cab from Central Park South once dinner ends. Parlor rooms tucked inside a Murray Hill hotel: velvet curtains, tufted leather armchairs, wallpaper and a fireplace, and cocktails made with real care. Resy showed every slot from 9pm to 12:45am open for four on Saturday as of Nov 17, and it's now booked. If plans change, your backups, in the order you gave them:

On this week only

Exhibits and events running Nov 18–22, if you want to change things last minute
Opens Sat Nov 21 · Whitney

artport: A History of Internet Art

Opening day falls on your Saturday. 25 years of art made for the web, plus the world premiere of a live performance piece, Human Unreadable Act III, in the museum's theater on Nov 19, 21 and 22 (separate ticket).

Fits: Saturday morning, at the bottom of the High Line (it's a Plan B there).

whitney.org
Through Jan 31 · The Met

Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous

The Met's first major show on either painter, and the first big New York show on either in over 20 years. The husband and wife are hung side by side, so you see who influenced whom.

Fits: a rainy morning, any day. Buy tickets online to skip the ticket line.

metmuseum.org
Through Feb 27 · MoMA

Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio

About 210 objects from his Paris studio: the polished bronzes, the Endless Column pieces, his tools and his own photographs. Possible only because the Paris studio is closed for renovation.

Fits: Thursday instead of the Intrepid, or Friday morning if it rains. Timed tickets.

moma.org
Through Jan 4 · Radio City

Christmas Spectacular with the Rockettes

The longest run the show has ever had, with a new number this year. 90 minutes, no intermission, across the street from the Rockefeller rink.

In the plan: Saturday, 1:00pm matinee.

rockettes.com
Now open · Bryant Park & Union Sq

Holiday markets

Bryant Park's Winter Village is already in the plan for Thursday. The Union Square market (open since about Nov 12) is the craftier, less touristy one. Columbus Circle's doesn't open until Dec 1.

Optional: Bryant Park on Thursday afternoon. Union Square is the swap.

Urbanspace markets
Evenings · Chelsea Market

ARTECHOUSE: SUBMERGE

A digital-art room in Chelsea Market's old boiler room, with floor-to-ceiling projected worlds. Hour-long sessions, evenings only (Friday about 6–8pm, Saturday 6–10pm); confirm the run before you go.

Fits: an alternative if the Friendsgiving crowd wants an outing.

artechouse.com

Just missing it: Saks Fifth Avenue unveils its windows and light show on Monday Nov 23, the day after you fly home, and the Rockefeller tree is lit in early December. You'll see the tree going up, still under wraps.
